questions.prompt: What mainly gives raisins a longer shelf life than fresh grapes?
answers: Less natural sugar in the fruit
A thicker wax coating on the skin
questions.hint: Think about what you add to plump a raisin up again.
questions.explanation: Drying reduces available moisture and inhibits microbial growth. Abigail includes raisin cakes in provisions carried by donkeys, but the story does not explain drying or her reason for choosing them. This connection is presently too thin to count as ready.
questions.authorFinding: The food appears in the reading, but the passage adds little to the asked preservation inference. Replace or substantially strengthen pairing.
questions.concept: Raisin preservation by reduced available water

questions.prompt: When cream is churned into butter, what mainly gathers into clumps?
questions.hint: Think of the greasy mark a pat of butter leaves on paper.
questions.explanation: Churning disrupts membranes around fat droplets so they join into butter grains. Proteins surround the droplets but are not the main material forming butter; sugar remains dissolved, and whipped-in air is lost as butter forms. Proverbs uses an everyday cause-and-effect comparison to warn against provoking conflict.
questions.authorFinding: The verse names butter but not the component. Paid clue adds an observable property; test whether it earns its cost.

questions.prompt: Which step is excluded when making extra virgin olive oil?
questions.hint: Think of keeping the oil as it comes from the fruit.
questions.explanation: Extra virgin oil is a category of virgin oil obtained by physical methods, without refining. Washing, centrifugation and filtration are permitted. Micah describes pressing olives in a judgment against injustice: labor will not yield enjoyment of its products. The verse does not assign a modern oil grade.
questions.authorFinding: Negative stem needs playtest. Mechanical pressing is the specific bridge, but the reading cannot establish the full modern standard. Do not claim zero heat or that all mechanically obtained oil is extra virgin.
questions.concept: Extra virgin olive oil excludes refining
questions.coordinatorFinding: Pressing does not distinguish virgin from refined oils, which both start with extraction. As it comes from fruit hint may wrongly exclude permitted filtering/centrifugation. Refine pairing and hint.

questions.prompt: Which addition best complements wheat protein with a different amino acid balance?
questions.hint: Pair a cereal with a member of the bean family.
questions.explanation: Legumes and grains can complement their proportions of essential amino acids. Lentils are the legume among these choices; the others are cereal grains. The passage includes all four choices in a rationed mixture, not an endorsed wellness recipe. A varied diet can supply amino acids across the day; the foods need not be eaten together.
questions.authorFinding: HOLD: mixture detail does not yet teach a useful inference; hint is mostly food-family classification. Do not imply each plant entirely lacks certain amino acids or turn siege rationing into health endorsement.

questions.prompt: Which gas builds pressure as grape juice ferments into wine?
questions.hint: It is also the gas that makes a sparkling drink fizz.
questions.explanation: Alcoholic fermentation converts sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide. The other gases are not the gas produced in this reaction. The bursting wineskin is a concrete pressure connection; the verse does not name the gas. Jesus gives the image while answering a question about fasting.
questions.authorFinding: Fizz clue adds another familiar observation but still requires gas identification. Test incremental value; the Bible reading itself only supplies pressure imagery.
